caption: The drawing consists of two technical views of a wooden chest rendered in fine pencil lines on a beige, lightly textured paper. The left side shows the "Front View" of the chest, which is rectangular with ornate carvings covering most of its visible surfaces. The carvings include swirling floral and vine patterns with two prominent rectangular panels on the left, each featuring what appears to be a stylized tree. A third panel is in the center, inscribed with the letters "MS," and a fourth panel on the right contains letters or a design partially covered by stylized scrollwork. Measurements in inches are detailed above and to the left of the chest, with various vertical and horizontal lines demarcating the chest’s dimensions. A faint indication of a "drawer" is marked in the lower section. On the right side of the drawing, the "Side View" shows the chest’s depth and construction, including a slightly projecting top and simple side panels with minimal detailing. At the bottom right corner, a title block provides identity details: it indicates this is a drawing of a "carved oak chest" from the "South Parlor, Withersfield House," attributed to the "Brooklyn Museum," and is labeled "#12306-1." Some light handwriting and editing marks are present on the paper throughout the drawing.
title: Chest
